Connect to foundations: Stars, gas, vacuum, and the forces of nature ↗ Compare solution assumptions and boundary data in the solution library ↗ 01From steady disks to evolving disks The alpha chapter examined steady accretion. Now let surface density evolve in a thin Keplerian disk. A fixed central mass dominates; omit winds, external supply and disk self-gravity. Radial velocity is positive outward. ∂Σ∂t+1r∂∂r(rΣvr)=0, j=√(GMr) Subtract j times mass conservation from angular-momentum conservation to eliminate radial advection in favour of a stress gradient. A specified viscosity closes the model. 02Derive surface-density diffusion vr=−3Σr1/2∂∂r(νΣr1/2) ∂Σ∂t=3r∂∂r[r1/2∂∂r(νΣr1/2)] ν represents effective transport, not necessarily molecular viscosity. Prescribe ν = ν₁(r/R₁)ᵞ with γ < 2 and no dependence on time or Σ. This differs from solving temperature and transport together in a general alpha disk. x=rR₁, β=2−γ, ts=R₁²3β²ν₁, T=1+tts 03Substitute a similarity solution Use zero torque at the origin, an infinite outer disk and the smooth initial profile implied below. Differentiating in τ = t/ts and y = xᵝ/T matches the powers of T and x on both sides of the PDE. Σ(r,t)=M₀β2πR₁²x−γT−(5/2−γ)/βexp(−xβT) This is an exact similarity solution for a particular initial profile, not for every disk. It can also provide useful late-time intuition for broader classes of initial data. Md=M₀T−1/(2β), Rc=R₁T1/β Ṁin=M₀2βtsT−(5/2−γ)/β 04Inward accretion and outward spreading vr=3νr[βxβT−12] rturn=R₁[T2β]1/β Flow is inward below rturn and outward above it. The plotted 2πr²Σ/M₀ is mass per log radius normalized to initial mass; colours denote epochs, not tracked particle trajectories. Playback advances t/ts uniformly. Physical R₁ and ν₁ specify ts for conversion; screen seconds are not disk time. 05Account for lost mass and retained angular momentum Substitution y = xᵝ/T gives the disk mass integral. Angular momentum carries an extra √r factor; spreading exactly compensates the decreasing mass. J=2π√(GM)∫0∞Σr3/2dr=constant Maccreted=M₀−Md, −dMddt=Ṁin Accreted material has j → 0 at the origin, leaving angular momentum in the disk. Finite inner radii, stellar spin or winds change the budget. M₀ ≪ M lets us neglect the accreted mass in the central gravitational field. The plots recompute this analytic solution, checked against the PDE and mass/angular-momentum budgets. They do not reproduce all initial profiles or figures in the original paper. CHECK YOUR UNDERSTANDING Pause and work it out. For γ = 1, increase T from 1 to 4. How do disk mass, characteristic radius, central accretion rate and angular momentum change? Show the answer and reasoning Mass halves, characteristic radius grows by four, and central accretion rate falls by eight. Total disk angular momentum stays constant for this infinite outer disk with a zero-torque boundary at the origin.
